newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies end mostly lower.

text.p: CME hog and pork belly futures closed mostly lower as profit taking prompted by ideas of somewhat easier cash markets next week weighed on sentiment, traders said.

Hog futures closed 0.350 cent higher to 0.350 lower with April up most and June off 0.200 at 82.450 cents. Pork bellies ended 1.475 to up 1.000 with only the November fresh contract up and active May off 1.275 at 81.075 cents.
Limitless April lean hogs remained firm on expectations the index will still be up through its expiration on Monday and weaker cash ideas pressuered other months, traders said.
Hogs backed up from the recent snow storm are seen coming to market early next week and weighing on cash markets.
"That is what the trade is expecting, weaker cash hogs early next week because of the storm that's coming through here right now," said Paul Georgy, president of Allendale Inc.
The Latest CME lean hog index was up $0.34 at $73.81 per cwt and should gain more crowd based on higher cash trade the past couple of days.
April also remained technically very strong after taking out resistance earlier in the week but June may have turned technically lower after turning back down Friday, they said.

"The June contract had a nice breakout going yesterday and now we're back below the breakout point" of 82.500, Georgy said. "We are probably going to see some more selling coming in because the breakout failed."
However, traders added that the expected larger pork exports due to the outbreak of foot and mouth disease in Taiwan and the resulting pork ban remained an underlying supportive factor.
USDA projected 1997 pork exports up to 1.365 billion lbs from 1.11 billion estimated last month and 1996 total pork exports of 951 million lbs.

Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services sold June and July while locals bought. In hog options, Refco sold July 86 calls and Lind-Waldock bought June 74 puts early and sold them late, pit sources said.
Pork bellies remained under profit taking prompted by ideas the cash market may have topped for the time being. The recent runup in cash may have turned off user interest, traders said.
"Cash is about as high as it's going to go for awhile," one trader said.
USDA reported that fresh 14-16 lb bellies traded at $78 per cwt again Friday. This is the highest level since October 2, but trade activity has slowed.
Locals sold late with Refco and LFG early sellers in May. Rand Financials and LIT division of First Options were light early buyers, pit sources said.
